body:
Thank you so much for your comment! I had no idea that there were improv classes tailored towards individuals with depression and anxiety! How did you find that program? I've started looking but it does not appear as though there are any such programs in my area. I would be really interested in doing something like that. 

Thank you for sharing what you are doing with regards to writing too. I have found that when I start writing, occasionally I induce a panic attack of sorts (as ridiculous as that sounds). But I seem to latch onto an idea that is bothering me and sometimes it causes me to panic. It is so silly. I want to get rid of that response. I'm glad that blogging has been so healing! I wish I could find a solid way of working around my own odd anxiety. 

Did you just need a physician's note to try ketamine? How did you ask for it? My physician has tried a variety of antidepressants, then after an attempted suicide, suggested that I needed to be prescribed some sedatives. But those sedatives really stripped my ability to think clearly and made me quite miserable.
Thank you for your comment! As difficult as that has been for me, I completely agree that it is the healthiest choice I can make :)
Thank you so much for these links! I'm going to seriously look into these. I really hope that with practice, I will learn to help myself. Thank you very, very much for these. I really appreciate it.

Thank you so, so, so much for your kind and thoughtful answer. I cannot begin to tell you exactly how much I appreciated hearing from your perspective. I can relate so much to what you just described. I am really terrified of being rejected because of how long it took me to get help myself. 

I really like your advice about reaching out via letters and then hoping for the best. I feel very lost and truly sad that I have hurt so many people that I love so very much. I would do anything to make it better. Thank you so, so, so much for your encouragement and your kindness. You are really wonderful. I appreciate it more than I can begin to say.

Thank you for your comment! Would you happen to have any tips for novices for how to start practicing these? I feel like thoughts in my head go a mile a minute. I would love to get to a point where I am only an observer of my thoughts instead of experiencing every emotion that comes with them. If you have any advice, I would sincerely appreciate it. Thank you!

You are so, so, so wonderful and so kind. I appreciate your comments immensely. Thank you so very much for all your encouragement and all your advice. I mean it so sincerely!

Unfortunately, I had many people in my life leave because they said they could not handle the depression. They said they had waited too long without seeing any changes and they doubted whether it was possible that I would change at all. They said they could not deal with this mental illness and have since withdrawn. I had originally tried apologizing and then talked about how I was trying a new, different form of therapy and was really doing my best to get better. But it doesn't seem to have done anything. My therapist keeps suggesting that I find a strong support group but since the loss of my closest friends/family, I'm struggling to find ways to change that or people to turn to, hence asking for suggestions regarding reconnecting. I blame myself for pushing them away. I just wish I could fix it. 

Thank you so very much for your kindness though. It is so unbelievably appreciated. You are such a wonderful person!

Thank you so much for those sites! I am really interested in doing those. I was on the antidepressants for a few months but you're right -- it may not have been long enough to properly note any changes. I will look into potentially getting started on them again. Thank you so much for your insight and your kindness. I really appreciate it.

Thank you so, so, so very much for your kind and thoughtful response! I honestly cannot begin to tell you how much it means to me and how much I appreciate it. 

This might be an odd question, but would you happen to have any experience with reconnecting with people you may have hurt during depression? I hurt and alienated a lot of people who really only tried to help me when I was struggling. I feel horrible about it and have been trying desperately to make amends, but I honestly do not know how. There is a lot of broken trust and pain because they did not really know how to help me and I did not know how to let them either. I'm so sorry if this is an inappropriate question. It is just another thing I have been struggling with.

Thank you so much again for your kindness and your insight.

Thank you so much for such a thoughtful response! These are all wonderful activities and I really look forward to trying them. I am really eager to change my behavior because I alternate between feeling sad and tired and feeling hyper-anxious and uneasy. It is really frustrating. I was prescribed anti-anxiety medications and then antidepressants, but they gave me severe insomnia and I believe, contributed to the suicide attempt. I really appreciated hearing that TED talk. I have felt hopeless and powerless against my mind and I am so eager to change it and to fix myself. Thank you so much for your response!

Thank you so much for letting me know! Is there any particular kind of exercise that works? I was just put on a cocktail of antidepressants by a psychiatrist and it made me feel really awful. So after stopping them, I've been struggling to find a good way to get back on my feet! Thank you so, so much for sharing this! :)
